label: Claude Haiku 5.5
output:
Hey @Mikaela, good on you for asking. We're a fair way into it now so I can give you the real version.

Short answer: it's cost us some milk and we've had a couple of real stuff-ups, but I wouldn't go back.

We're milking 290 cows, mostly 3-way crosses. We started 10 in 7 on 21 Sept, after mating started. We skip the afternoon milkings on Tuesday, Thursday, Saturday and Sunday, so that's four once-a-days a week and mornings are at 5.15 every day.

The hit on production is around 6% down on the same weeks last year, going by the Fonterra app. Our rep said to expect 8-10%, so we've done a bit better than that, but it's still money. You'll be giving up milk.

Cells did jump. SCC went from about 110k to around 180k in the first three weeks. It's back down to about 135k now, but that first bit was a worry. Our vet was keeping a close eye on it.

The good bits: lame cows are way down. We've got 4 on the lame list now against 11 this time last year. That matters because our back paddocks are a 1.8km walk and the cows were doing it twice a day with fewer afternoon trips, so I reckon the shorter walks have helped.

Cows came round quicker than I expected. They bellowed at the gate for about 4 days and then settled fine.

The hours are the real win. Dave and I went to Hamilton to see the grandkids on a skipped Sunday arvo, which was our first Sunday off in spring in 20-odd years. Kieran, our 2IC, said it's the first spring he hasn't wanted to quit by October. For us that's worth the 6%, honestly.

The bad bit: we had a heifer go bad with mastitis on one of the skipped arvos. We didn't pick it up until the next morning and lost a quarter. That's on us, not the system, but it does mean you can't get slack. You have to be on your game with teat spraying and checking cows on the skip days, or it bites you. If your people aren't reliable about that, I'd think hard before starting.

On Tom's knees: if they're bad, the arvos off will help more than anything. Being on your feet less is the main thing.

If you want to see the numbers, come along to the field day at the Kerrisons on the 19th. I'll have the shed rosters and milk numbers with me, and you can see what the days actually look like. Grant's running it at 10am, and Shaun says park along the race, not on the lawn.

Or ring me if you want to talk it through. That's easier than texting with these thumbs.

Bev
